text:
Dream House / Seiro Arquitectos

Some houses overlook the sea, while others allow you to live at its pace. Casa Ensueño does the latter: a residence conceived as a succession of open, protected, and serene spaces, where the architecture accompanies the shifting light, the movement of the air, and the constant presence of the Pacific Ocean.

title: Cabeceiras do Aricanduva Municipal Natural Park / Natureza Urbana
text:
Cabeceiras do Aricanduva Municipal Natural Park / Natureza Urbana

Located in Cidade Tiradentes, in the eastern zone of São Paulo, the Nascentes Hub of the Cabeceiras do Aricanduva Municipal Natural Park spans an area of approximately 96,000 m², featuring remnants of the Atlantic Forest and the headwaters of the Aricanduva River basin. Developed by Natureza Urbana in partnership with the Department of Implementation, Projects, and Works of the Municipal Secretariat for the Green and the Environment, the project brings the local community closer to this natural heritage while establishing a transition between the neighborhood and the preservation area.

title: Madre Culebra Cabin / Taller Viga Maestra
text:
Madre Culebra Cabin / Taller Viga Maestra

In a clearing of the native forest of the Las Trancas Valley, at the foot of the Andes Mountains, the Madre Culebra Refuge is installed, seeking to occupy the territory with the least possible alteration. Surrounded by trees and facing the extreme conditions of the mountains, the house is conceived as a vertical, compact, and protected shelter, designed for family and friends to gather.

title: Anchorage Road Artist Studio / Ballman Khapalova
text:
Anchorage Road Artist Studio / Ballman Khapalova

The goal was to create an economical and efficient building that opened up to north and south light for different tasks, in turn maximizing connection to the surrounding landscape and creating a private, protected space for creative work.

title: North Boulder Library / WORKac
text:
North Boulder Library / WORKac

The Boulder Public Library issued an open Request for Proposal (RFP) in 2018 for a new branch library in North Boulder, a project the community had anticipated for over two decades. The RFP called for an "iconic" building, which many competitors interpreted as a visually striking design. However, WORKac www.work.ac - the architecture firm based in New York City and led by Amale Andraos and Dan Wood - proposed a vision where the library's iconic status would stem from its sustainability and its positive impact on the community and environment.

title: Modern and Mexican: Mario Pani’s CUPA Housing Complex in Mexico City
text:
Modern and Mexican: Mario Pani’s CUPA Housing Complex in Mexico City

In 1947, Mexico's General Directorate of Civil Pensions commissioned young architect Mario Pani to design 200 houses for government employees on a recently acquired plot of land in Colonia del Valle, then a distant neighborhood on the outskirts of Mexico City. Rather than following the original guidelines, Pani proposed a 13-story housing complex with extensive green areas, communal spaces, and more than a thousand apartments. Drawing on Le Corbusier's functionalist principles, the architect created a project that opened in 1949 and would become a landmark in Latin American modern architecture.

title: The Cloud House / Peter Morris Architects
text:
The Cloud House / Peter Morris Architects

Architect Peter Morris reveals his most remarkable achievement to date: 'The Cloud House'. Drawing inspiration from the eccentric, Grade I-listed St Martin's Church opposite, and the castle-like Grade II-listed school next door, the property brings a touch of fairytale flamboyance to its north London surroundings. Its pale-pink exteriors, oversized arches, and duck-egg blue metalwork bring joyfulness and colour to the eclectic local architecture, with an interior featuring pale turquoise painted epoxy floors, pink and white marquee stripes on walls and ceilings, and an emerald green and white striped kitchen with pale pink Plykea worktops.

title: The Nordic Pavilion Explores Traditional Craft Through "Painted Matter" at the 2027 Venice Architecture Biennale
text:
The Nordic Pavilion Explores Traditional Craft Through "Painted Matter" at the 2027 Venice Architecture Biennale

The National Museum of Norway has announced Painted Matter as the title of Norway's contribution to the 20th International Architecture Exhibition of the Venice Biennale, scheduled to take place from May 8 to November 21, 2027. Developed by Oslo-based practice Kastler Skjeseth Architects, the exhibition will be presented at the Nordic Pavilion and will explore the role of traditional decorative painting techniques in contemporary architecture, with a focus on material use, architectural expression, and sustainability. The Nordic Pavilion, designed by Norwegian architect Sverre Fehn, is jointly owned by Norway, Sweden, and Finland. For the 2027 edition, the National Museum of Norway is responsible for organizing the Nordic contribution on behalf of Moderna Museet in Stockholm and the Architecture and Design Museum in Helsinki.

title: UN-Habitat and ICPAC Launch a Practical Guide to Help Cities Prepare for El Niño
text:
UN-Habitat and ICPAC Launch a Practical Guide to Help Cities Prepare for El Niño

El Niño is a natural climate pattern expected to peak from October 2026 through March 2027. It is characterized by a strong impact on global weather patterns, bringing floods, droughts, heat waves and storms to different regions. On November 5, 2026, the United Nations Human Settlements Programme (UN-Habitat) and the Climate Prediction and Applications Centre (ICPAC) of the Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD) launched a short practical guide for city governments to help them prepare for the upcoming season. The guide offers considerations applicable to different climate regions, but it is framed by IGAD in the context of preparedness, anticipatory action and resilience in the Horn of Africa (Djibouti, Eritrea, Ethiopia, Kenya, Somalia, South Sudan, Sudan and Uganda). Its aim is to offer actionable guidance to improve urban resilience, protect vulnerable communities and reduce the impacts of climate-related hazards.

title: Miami Architecture City Guide: 22 Projects Shaping Tropical Density on the Atlantic Coast
text:
Miami Architecture City Guide: 22 Projects Shaping Tropical Density on the Atlantic Coast

Stretching along the Atlantic coast at the southern tip of Florida, Miami is often introduced through postcard views of beaches, palm trees, and glass towers facing the water. Yet, behind this familiar image lies a city shaped by migration, tourism, and real estate cycles, where architecture has repeatedly been used to project new identities and reinvent the urban landscape. From early resort hotels and the Art Deco façades of South Beach to experimental high-rises and cultural institutions on the bay, the built environment offers a way to read how Miami negotiates climate, economy, and everyday life.

text:
Itan House / atelier kọ

Ìtàn is the Yoruba word for story or history, and this house in Cotonou has a long one. It belongs to an Afro-Brazilian architectural tradition associated with families who returned from Brazil to the coast of Benin, with its pink walls, breeze-block screens, and louvered shutters.

title: House in Akashi / Tato Architects

House in Akashi / Tato Architects

title: HaloPlaza Hangzhou Vanke Mixed-use Complex / Nikken Sekkei
text:
HaloPlaza Hangzhou Vanke Mixed-use Complex / Nikken Sekkei

By revitalizing a neglected canal, we created a fresh and vibrant urban environment and planned a continuous and open public space along the waterfront. Above this public space, multiple functions — including offices, retail, cultural, and serviced apartments — are vertically layered together with elevated open spaces. This composition pursues a new form of mixed-use complex in which multiple buildings are stacked like second and third "ground planes." The layered open spaces are connected to the ground-level public spaces through atrium voids, designed as "urban voids" where a variety of activities emerging from the canal unfold in a three-dimensional manner.

title: Casa Lambda / Guillem Carrera
text:
Casa Lambda / Guillem Carrera

Lambda House is located on the southeastern edge of the urban center of Castellvell del Camp, where the consolidated residential fabric gives way to the agricultural fields of the Barranc del Picarany. This transitional setting, slightly removed from the urban continuity, establishes a direct visual relationship with the landscape, granting the house a peripheral yet connected position to the natural environment. The area is characterized by medium-sized plots of diverse shapes, mostly occupied by single-family homes with gardens, resulting from an urban development that expanded between the late 20th and early 21st centuries in the intermediate space between Reus and Castellvell del Camp.
